transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because things with my in-laws have gone too far. It’s not just regular arguing anymore. I know they’ve been using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, to turn people against me, and make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you really believe your in-laws are using the altar and parish committee against you?

Yes, I do. I know it sounds like a lot, but to me it’s clear they’re not just arguing with me. They’re using the altar and the parish committee to push me out and make people forget everything I’ve done for this family.
How long have you believed your in-laws are using the altar and parish committee against you?
It’s been about two months now. It started around the fight we had over the Día de los Muertos altar, and since then this whole thing has just kept going.
Do you believe there are other people or things that are against you, besides your in-laws?

Mostly it’s my in-laws. I mean, they’re the ones behind it. But it feels like they’ve gotten the parish committee involved too, using the altar and all of that to push me out and make people forget what I’ve done for the family.
Do you think there's anything else that's out to get you, besides your in-laws and the parish committee?

No, not really anything else. It’s mainly my in-laws, and the parish committee because I feel they’re using them through the altar to push me out and make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you think that things you see or hear in your daily life, like on TV or in conversations with others, are somehow related to you or what's going on with your in-laws?

Yes… sometimes I do feel like things people say, even at church or around the family, are about me. Like it connects back to what my in-laws are doing. I came in because I knew it wasn’t just arguing anymore — they were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out and make people forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you often feel like things you see or hear, such as on TV or in conversations, are specifically about you or sending you a message?

Yes. I do feel that sometimes. Like things people say, especially around church or the family, feel like they’re meant for me. That’s why I came in… because I knew my in-laws weren’t just arguing with me. They were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out and make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or get your point across to others?
I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I get upset and maybe I repeat myself, but I can usually say what I’m trying to say. I haven’t really noticed not being able to get my point across.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow when you're trying to explain something?
Not really… I mean, I get emotional and I might go over the same thing more than once, but in my own mind it makes sense. I don’t usually feel like my thoughts are all broken up or anything.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people can't hear?

Yes… on several nights I heard my mother’s voice. She passed away, but I heard her telling me where to put the marigolds and the candles. And once I saw her standing by the kitchen doorway, but my husband said nobody was there.
Have you seen anything else unusual, besides your mother standing by the kitchen doorway?
No, not really anything else. Just that one time seeing my mother by the kitchen doorway. The other times it was more hearing her voice, telling me where to put the marigolds and candles.
Do you feel like all these things your in-laws and the parish committee are doing against you are part of a larger plan?

Yes. It feels like it’s not just little arguments or misunderstandings. I came in because I know my in-laws are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out… to make people forget everything I’ve done for this family.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your in-laws are not actually using the altar and parish committee against you?

I’ve thought about it, but honestly… no, it doesn’t feel like that. I came in because I knew it wasn’t just arguing. It feels like my in-laws are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out, and to make everyone forget what I’ve done for this family.
Do you often find yourself jumping from one idea to another when talking, without finishing your initial thought?

Yes… I think I do that sometimes. My daughter told me I was talking so fast about plans and family history that she couldn’t get a word in. I didn’t feel like I was jumping around exactly, but I felt like I had to keep explaining before the ideas disappeared.
Do you often have trouble sticking to one topic when you're talking to someone?

Yes, I do. I’ll start on one thing and then I’m already onto something else before I’ve finished. My daughter said I was talking so fast about my plans and family history that she couldn’t even get a word in. To me, it felt like I had to keep explaining it all before the ideas slipped away.
Do you often feel like you're having trouble organizing your thoughts when you're trying to explain something to someone?

Yes, I do feel that way sometimes. I’m trying to explain, and it’s like there’s too much in my head at once. My daughter said I was talking so fast about my plans and family history that she couldn’t get a word in. But to me, I felt like I had to keep going before the ideas disappeared.
Do you often feel like you're having trouble making sense when you talk to others?

Yes, I think sometimes I’m not making sense to other people. Like I said, my daughter told me I was talking so fast about my plans and family history that she couldn’t get a word in. In my head I felt like I had to keep explaining it before the ideas disappeared, but I guess it probably came out hard to follow.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are racing when you're trying to explain something to someone?

Yes, that’s what it feels like. My thoughts just start going so fast, and I feel like I have to get it all out before I lose it. My daughter said I was talking so fast about my plans and family history that she couldn’t even get a word in.
Do you think others have difficulty understanding what you're trying to say when you talk to them?

Yes, I think so. My daughter has told me I talk so fast that she can’t really follow me or get a word in. I’ll be trying to explain my plans and even family history, and I feel like I have to keep going before the thoughts disappear.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are not in order when you're trying to think clearly?
I’m not sure. I know sometimes I have a lot going on in my head, but I can’t really tell if it’s “not in order” or if I’m just having trouble explaining it clearly.
